title: Hush · A quiet password generator for the Mac menu bar
description: Press a shortcut and a strong password lands quietly on your clipboard. Hush is fully offline, stores nothing, hides copies from clipboard managers and clears them after 30 seconds. Free and open source under GPL-3.0.
hero_title:
Press a shortcut.
A strong password
lands quietly.
hero_lead: Hush is a password generator for the Mac menu bar. Fully offline, it stores no passwords; copies are hidden from clipboard managers and cleared after 30 seconds.
stat2_desc: website password rules, built in and offline
stat3_desc: network requests: the sandbox has no network access
modes_lead: Every secret comes from the system's secure random source with uniform sampling. Strength is computed exactly: rules like “every character type at least once” and PIN weak-pattern filtering are subtracted honestly, never inflated.
mode_phrase_note: 68 bits · EFF word list · easy to type
mode_pin_note: Avoids 123456, dates and other weak patterns
mode_say_note: 64 bits · easy to read out loud
kb_lead: The panel never steals focus, so the app you were in stays in front. Press ⌘↩ to paste straight into the field you were typing in.
kb_more: Click any character to re-roll just that one, or drag the password into another app.
mb_title: A mini generator in the menu bar
mb_lead: Click: generate and copy instantly. Right-click: see the password first, switch modes, change the length, pick a preset, then copy.
after_title:
What happens after,
already taken care of.
clip_lead: Marked as concealed, so Maccy, Paste and Raycast never record it. Cleared on a timer, but only if the clipboard still holds that password, so nothing you copy later is lost.
site_lead: Type an address and Hush follows that site's password requirements: maximum length, allowed symbols, repeat limits. 471 rules from Apple's open data, looked up offline.
presets_lead: Save the settings you use most as presets, each with its own global shortcut that copies without opening a panel. Export them as JSON to share one set of rules with your team.
large_lead: Typing it into a TV or a router? Press ⌘L. Guests need the Wi-Fi? Press ⌘K and they scan to join. The code is generated on your Mac.
privacy_title:
A password generator
should leave nothing behind.
privacy_lead: These are not settings; they are promises written into the code. All of it is public, and the sandbox has exactly two entitlements: the sandbox itself, and the file you pick to import or export.
p1_desc: The sandbox has no network entitlement. Website rules ship inside the app; Check for Updates simply opens a web page in your browser.
p2_desc: Passwords are never written to disk. Temporary history lives in memory and is wiped after 5 minutes, on lock, sleep or quit.
p3_desc: The clipboard clears 30 seconds after copying by default, hidden from clipboard managers. Or clear it right away.
p4_desc: GPL-3.0 licensed, every line on GitHub. Randomness comes only from the system's secure source, backed by statistical tests.
dev_title: For people who write code, too.
url_lead: Call Hush from Alfred, Raycast or a script. It copies by default, and says exactly which parameter is wrong if one is.
sc_lead: Two actions, Generate Password and Generate with Preset, return the password to the next step and can copy it too.
d1_desc: Light and dark follow the system, or pick one. A single cobalt accent: digits in cobalt, symbols in grey, so they are easy to tell apart.
d2_desc: General, Privacy, Presets, Appearance, Advanced and Developer, all in one window, each option saying what it does.
d3_desc: The interface follows your system language, fully translated into Simplified Chinese and English. VoiceOver even reads passwords character by character: “capital Q, digit 7”.
closing_sub: Free · Open source · Offline · macOS 14 or later
install_note: Signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple: unzip, move it to Applications and open. Hush never goes online, so it does not update itself; download new releases here.

pv_description: Hush collects nothing and sends nothing anywhere. How the Hush app and this website handle information.
pv_summary: In one sentence: Hush collects no data, and cannot — the app runs in a sandbox with no network access.
pv_body:
The Hush app (Mac App Store and GitHub versions)

Data we collect

None. Hush has no analytics, tracking, advertising, crash reporting or accounts. The app runs in the macOS sandbox without the network entitlement, so it cannot send data to any server.

What stays on your Mac

  • Settings and presets such as length, character types, shortcuts and your own presets, stored in the app's sandbox container (macOS preferences) only to remember your choices. They never contain passwords.
  • Generated passwords are never written to disk. The optional temporary history lives in memory only, holds at most 10 items, and is wiped after 5 minutes, on screen lock, on sleep and when you quit.
  • The clipboard: when you copy a password, Hush puts it on the system clipboard marked as concealed and transient so clipboard managers skip it, and clears it after a delay (only if the clipboard still holds that password).

Permissions

  • Files you choose: only when you import or export presets, Hush reads or writes the single file you pick in an Open or Save panel.
  • Accessibility (GitHub version only): used to send one ⌘V keystroke to the front app for “Paste directly” (⌘↩). It does not read other apps' content. The Mac App Store version does not include this feature and never asks for this permission.

Sharing with third parties

None. Hush contains no third-party SDKs. The built-in website password rules come from Apple's public data, ship inside the app and are looked up on your Mac.

“Check for Updates” (GitHub version only)

Opens the releases page on GitHub in your default browser. Hush itself never checks online. The Mac App Store version is updated through the App Store.

This website (hushpass.fyi)

This site sets no cookies, runs no analytics or tracking scripts and loads nothing from third parties, fonts included. It is hosted on Cloudflare Pages; like any web host, Cloudflare may process access logs such as IP addresses for security and abuse prevention, as described in the Cloudflare Privacy Policy. Downloads are served by GitHub, under the GitHub Privacy Statement.

Children's privacy

Hush collects no personal information from anyone, including children.

Changes and contact

If this policy changes, this page and the effective date above will be updated; the history is on GitHub. Questions are welcome in GitHub Issues.
